docs.title: Namespaces
docs.text:
Warehouses with thousands of schemas need short claims. A USE line sets the default namespace for every following line of the same document, until the next USE:

USE analytics.shop
ROWS orders VALUE >=1000                               # analytics.shop.orders
JOIN orders.customer_id -> crm.customers.id MATCH >=99%  # right side: analytics.crm.customers
USE staging
ROWS orders VALUE >=1000                               # staging.orders

USE produces no outcome. It is reserved only as the first token of a line.

docs.title: How a ref is resolved
docs.text:
A table ref has up to three slots, catalog, schema and table, filled from the right. A column ref has one more part, the column, which is always last. Missing leading slots are filled from the USE namespace; this applies to every ref of the claim, including the right side of a JOIN edge. Slots still missing are left empty and the connection's defaults apply when the probe runs.

The fully resolved ref is part of the claim's semantic hash, so USE shop + ROWS orders and ROWS shop.orders are the same fact. Connection defaults are unknown when a claim is analysed, so they are not.

docs.title: What the slots mean on each warehouse
docs.text:
dialect catalog schema table max table parts bigquery project dataset table 3 snowflake database schema table 3 redshift, postgres database schema table 3 duckdb database schema table 3 databricks catalog schema table 3 tsql database schema table 3 trino catalog schema table 3 mysql, clickhouse — database table 2 oracle — schema (owner) table 2

A resolved table ref with more parts than its dialect accepts is refused when the SQL is rendered (FL505), for example analytics.shop.orders on MySQL. A ref of more than four parts, or a USE that would make one, is FL302.

docs.title: Case
docs.text: An unquoted name is written unquoted, so the warehouse applies its own case rules, including configuration-dependent ones such as MySQL's lower_case_table_names or a SQL Server collation. A quoted name keeps its exact case. If an unquoted name is a reserved word of the dialect, FactLang quotes it after applying the case the warehouse would have applied (upper on Snowflake and Oracle, lower on Postgres and Redshift), which is what the unquoted name would have resolved to.

docs.title: Standard verbs
docs.text:
The standard pack (standard, version 1.0) has 19 verbs in five groups. This page explains what each one measures and when it passes; the generated verb reference lists every attribute, operator and example.

  • Structure facts (EXISTS, TYPE): does the table or column exist, and what type family is it? Answered from the catalog.
  • Data-quality facts (ROWS, NULLS, DEAD, UNIQUE, FANOUT, VALUES, RANGE, PATTERN, FRESH): how many rows, how many NULLs, which values, how fresh.
  • Relationship facts (JOIN): do the keys of one table find their match in another?
  • Answer facts (COUNT, DISTINCT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX): the numbers an agent states in an answer, checked against the warehouse.
  • Semantic facts (NOTE): a statement no query can establish, kept for the record.

Each verb is one Contract: a plan (the measurement), a derive step that turns measured rows into named facts, and a decide predicate over those facts. A fact the data cannot support is None, and a predicate over None is undecidable, so the verdict is no_data, never a pass.

docs.title: Structure facts
docs.text:
Answered from the catalog; no data is scanned.

EXISTS orders
EXISTS orders COLUMN shipped_at
TYPE orders.amount IS decimal

EXISTS t COLUMN c names a column with an attribute rather than as t.c, because a.b could equally be schema a, table b. TYPE compares the column's type family, one of integer decimal float string boolean date timestamp time bytes json array struct other. Each dialect maps its native type names onto these families (wrappers such as Nullable(…) are unwrapped first, and a scale-0 decimal such as NUMBER(38,0) is an integer).

When the catalog cannot answer (no catalog, or the warehouse would not say), the verdict is no_data with "catalog could not answer": never a pass, never a fail.

docs.title: Data-quality facts
docs.text:
Measured over every row that matches the claim's filter.

verb example passes when ROWS ROWS orders VALUE >=1000 row_count satisfies the comparison NULLS NULLS orders.shipped_at RATE <=5% null_rate satisfies the comparison DEAD DEAD orders.legacy_flag every value is NULL (null_rate == 1) UNIQUE UNIQUE order_items.order_id WITH [line_no] no key is held by more than one row FANOUT FANOUT order_items.order_id MAX_PER_KEY <=50 the busiest key's row count satisfies the comparison VALUES VALUES orders.status IN ['paid', 'open'] every non-NULL value is declared RANGE RANGE orders.amount BETWEEN [0, 10000] min and max lie inside the closed range PATTERN PATTERN customers.email LIKE '%@%.%' RATE >=99% the share matching satisfies the comparison FRESH FRESH events.created_at WITHIN 24h the newest value is no older than the duration

The exact definitions, because these are the product:

null_rate (row_count − non_null) / row_count; None (so no_data) for an empty table. UNIQUE and FANOUT Rows with a NULL in any key column are excluded before grouping. A composite key (WITH [...]) is grouped by its columns, never concatenated. duplicate_keys counts the distinct keys held by more than one row; max_rows_per_key is the busiest key's count. VALUES The column is compared as text, case-sensitively, after TRIM; numbers in the list are written in canonical form (1, 2.5). NULLs are excluded. SPLIT ':' compares only the part before the first separator, so other: customer moved counts as other. ALLOW <=1% tolerates a share of undeclared rows. Facts include undeclared_rows, coverage (declared rows / non-NULL rows) and top_undeclared, the most frequent undeclared values with their counts (at most 20, ranked by count then value; the counts themselves are exact). An empty list, IN [], declares nothing, so every value is undeclared and top_undeclared is the exact top of the column. RANGE Bounds are numbers or typed dates/timestamps, [low, high] inclusive. DATE bounds over a TIMESTAMP column mean the half-open UTC interval [low 00:00Z, high + 1 day 00:00Z), so BETWEEN [DATE '2025-01-01', DATE '2025-01-31'] includes every instant of 31 January. PATTERN SQL LIKE (% and _), case-folded on both sides, over non-NULL values: match_rate = matching / non_null. FRESH One query returns the column's maximum and the server's clock; Python computes age_seconds. A TIMESTAMP without zone and a DATE are read as UTC (a date is its midnight). A non-temporal column gives no_data ("not a temporal value"); an empty table gives no_data.

docs.title: Relationship facts
docs.text:
JOIN orders.customer_id -> customers.id CARD N:1 MATCH >=99%
JOIN order_items.order_id -> orders.order_id WITH [shop_id] TO [shop_id] MATCH >=99%
JOIN events.session_id -> sessions.id MATCH >=99% COVERAGE >=50% CAST string

MATCH is decided on match_rate: matched distinct non-NULL left keys over distinct non-NULL left keys. NULL left keys are excluded; their share is a NULLS claim, not a join claim. Without CAST, keys are compared in their native types, and the analyser warns (FL312) when the catalog shows two different type families; CAST <family> casts every key part on both sides.

Beyond match_rate, a JOIN reports:

  • coverage: matched distinct right keys over distinct non-NULL right keys, how much of the right side the left side reaches. COVERAGE >=50% decides on it.
  • row_match_rate: left rows whose key matched, over left rows with a key.
  • fan_in: left rows per distinct left key.
  • distinct_left, distinct_right, matched, left_non_null, matched_left_rows.
  • max_left_per_key and max_right_per_key when CARD is given. CARD N:1 requires every right key to occur at most once, 1:1 both sides, 1:N the left side.

All of them are None, never 0, when undecidable (for example an empty right side). Composite keys use WITH [...] for further left columns and TO [...] for the matching right columns; both must be present (FL304) with equal lengths (FL309). A key tuple with a NULL part is excluded on its side. A filter on JOIN applies to the left table only.

docs.title: Answer facts
docs.text:
These are the numbers agents put in answers.

COUNT opportunities VALUE ==1717 WHERE stage = 'Churned'
DISTINCT orders.customer_id VALUE ==512
SUM orders.amount VALUE ==209000 TOLERANCE 1%
AVG orders.amount VALUE ==104.5 ABS_TOLERANCE 0.01
MIN orders.amount VALUE >=0
MAX orders.placed_on VALUE <=DATE '2026-12-31'

TOLERANCE is relative to the stated value (1% of it); ABS_TOLERANCE is an absolute band; they are mutually exclusive. With neither, the comparison is exact:

  • Results arrive from the warehouse as Decimal where the driver allows, and are compared as Decimal, exactly: SUM … VALUE ==0.3 means 0.3, not 0.30000000000000004.
  • When either side is a float (a DOUBLE column, or a driver that returns floats), == uses math.isclose(rel_tol=1e-9, abs_tol=1e-9), because the float was never exact to begin with.

SUM and AVG over no rows give value = None, so no_data, never 0. MIN and MAX accept typed dates and timestamps as well as numbers.

SQL Server and SUM/AVG

On tsql, SUM stays native: an INT sum beyond 2^31 is an arithmetic-overflow error, reported as an error verdict, never a wrong number (widening it would change a digit of some DECIMALs). AVG is taken over x + 0.0 because an integer AVG truncates; on a DECIMAL(38, s>0) that costs one fractional digit. Counts use COUNT_BIG.

docs.title: Semantic facts
docs.text:
NOTE orders.amount IS eur BECAUSE 'all prices are stored in euro'

A fact no query can establish. It parses, is analysed, gets a semantic hash and is reported as unprobeable with its reason. It is the reference example for modelling your own semantic facts.

docs.title: Verdicts
docs.text:
Every claim ends in exactly one of six verdicts:

verdict meaning pass measured, and the claim holds fail measured, and the claim does not hold no_data measured, but a fact the claim needs is undecidable (for example an empty table) error could not measure: the warehouse rejected the query, a timeout, the cost budget, a rendering error unprobeable a semantic fact by design (NOTE); recorded, never measured invalid did not get through the front end; the diagnostics say why

Two distinctions carry most of the weight:

no_data is not pass. A verb's derive step returns None for a fact the data cannot support: the NULL rate of an empty table, the sum of no rows, a join with no keys on one side. A predicate over None is undecidable, and undecidable propagates through and, or and not instead of collapsing to a pass. Otherwise a missing number coerced to 0 would satisfy <= 1 and pass while proving nothing.

error is not no_data. A warehouse that rejects the SQL is a defect to fix, not an absence of data. Execution problems carry an FL7xx code (FL700 failed, FL701 over the cost budget, FL702 timeout).

docs.title: How a verdict is decided
docs.text:
A contract measures, derives facts, then decides with a small predicate language: comparisons (Compare, CompareUsingClaimOp, Within for tolerances) combined with And, Or, Not and WhenClaimHas (apply a check only when the claim has an attribute). The language is deliberately weak: it serialises, and it explains itself. The explanation of every outcome names the numbers, such as match_rate 0.9765625 < 0.99.

Judging never raises. A contract that throws while deriving or deciding produces an error outcome for its own claim; one broken contract cannot sink a batch.

docs.title: The outcome object
docs.text:
Outcome is a frozen dataclass; to_dict() gives the JSON form.

field claim_text the claim as written canonical_text its canonical form (see fl.format) semantic_hash sha256:…, identical for the same fact however it is spelled verb the verb verdict a Verdict (a str enum: "pass", "fail", …) explanation one line naming the numbers facts every fact the verb derived, e.g. match_rate, coverage, top_undeclared evidence the SQL, parameters, dialect, tier and timings (see Evidence) diagnostics the claim's diagnostics as dictionaries

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
Checker.check(text) returns a Report: the ordered outcomes, every diagnostic raised while checking, and

  • report.verified: every claim that can be measured was measured and passed. It is True only when there is no fail, error, invalid or no_data outcome, no error diagnostic, and at least one outcome that is not unprobeable; an empty report is not verified. Use it when "the facts hold" is what you need to know.
  • report.ok: no fail, error or invalid outcome and no error diagnostic (a broken USE line, which has no outcome of its own, still makes the report not ok). It is the weaker flag: no_data and unprobeable outcomes, and an empty report, are still ok, so ok means "nothing was contradicted", not "everything was confirmed".
  • report.summary(): a count per verdict.
  • report.to_dict(), report.to_json(), report.to_markdown(); each carries both flags, and verified is the first key of the dict.

fl.check(text, connector=…) is the one-call form. It returns the Outcome when the text holds exactly one claim and the Report otherwise, so code that checks a document should use Checker.check, which always returns a Report with its document-level diagnostics.

docs.title: The command line
docs.text: factlang check turns verdicts into exit codes: 0 everything passed, 1 a claim failed, 2 invalid input, 3 errors or undecidable claims. Its last line says verified, ok, nothing verified (exit 0 with nothing measurable) or not verified (any non-zero exit), followed by the counts. See Command line.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
import factlang as fl

Everything in fl.__all__ is public API, and so is the __all__ of each public package: fl.ir, fl.sql, fl.connectors, fl.types, fl.syntax (factlang.syntax) and factlang.agent. Import from those paths; any other module path (factlang.semantics.…, factlang.ir.primitives, factlang.connectors.base, …) is internal and may move. The package follows SemVer from 0.1.0; the language itself is versioned separately (fl.LANGUAGE_VERSION == "1.0").

docs.text:
The following are public API under SemVer: no breaking change within a 0.x minor series. Libraries built on FactLang, schema profilers in particular, may depend on them.

The metric aliases (row_count non_null distinct_keys max_rows_per_key min_value max_value sum_value avg_value duplicate_keys server_now) are a wire format and do not change at all.

docs.title: One-call helpers
docs.text:
fl.check with a single claim returns an Outcome; with any other number it returns a Report. To get document-level diagnostics (a broken USE line, for instance) always use Checker.check, which returns a Report.

Report.verified is the flag to gate on: every outcome that is not UNPROBEABLE is PASS, there is at least one such outcome, and no error diagnostic was raised. Report.ok is weaker: it only rules out FAIL, ERROR and INVALID, so a report with NO_DATA outcomes, or with nothing measured at all, is ok but not verified.

docs.title: run_metadata
docs.text:
run_metadata(connector: Connector, sql: str, params: Sequence[Param] | Mapping[str, object] = (), *, timeout_s: float | None = None) -> QueryResult

Execute host-authored catalog metadata SQL through connector (spec 9.1, R8).

sql marks bind parameters with neutral {{name}} tokens, exactly as a rendered probe does, and params supplies them (Param objects, or a {name: value} mapping whose families are inferred). They are bound with the connector's paramstyle, never spliced. The guard (:func:check_metadata_sql) runs first and raises ExecutionError FL703 before anything executes. Execution, timeouts and error mapping are the connector's own (FL700/FL702). This is not a claim: it yields rows, never an Outcome. The probe passed to the connector has plan=None, and the rows keep the labels the warehouse returned (no lower-casing).

Through :class:~factlang.connectors.SQLAlchemyConnector, whose text() would read :word as a bind parameter even inside a string literal, every : in sql is escaped before binding, so literals such as 'a:b' and casts such as x::text reach the driver unchanged. A {{name}} token immediately after a : (x::{{t}}) cannot be bound by text(); neither can a token glued to a word character (a{{t}}, {{t}}b) or to another token ({{a}}{{b}}). SQLAlchemyConnector refuses those with FL700 before executing; separate them with a space.

T-SQL (tsql or an alias such as mssql/sqlserver/synapse/fabric, and, failing closed, any dialect with no native profile), where statements may need no separator: only a SELECT is accepted, and it runs wrapped as SELECT * FROM (<sql>) AS fl_meta_q. So there is no WITH/SHOW, no ORDER BY without TOP (SQL Server rejects it in a derived table), every result column needs a distinct name, and no quote character may appear: no string literals and no quoted identifiers (' " [ ]); pass values, and compare odd names, as parameters.

docs.title: DBAPIConnector
docs.text:
DBAPIConnector(connection: Any, dialect: str, paramstyle: str | None = None)

Executes probes on a PEP 249 connection.

paramstyle defaults to the driver module's paramstyle (else qmark). Each probe runs on a fresh cursor, closed afterwards. With timeout_s the statement is cancelled through the cursor's interrupt()/cancel() (duckdb, pyodbc), else the connection's (sqlite3, psycopg), when the driver has one, and reported as FL702.

Checker runs probes from several threads. Statements on one connection run concurrently only when that is safe: duckdb (cursor() is an independent duplicate connection), or a driver declaring PEP 249 threadsafety >= 2 whose cursors have their own cancel hook (trino). Otherwise they are serialised by one lock per connection object, shared by every connector wrapping it: a level-1 driver (pymysql, pyodbc; clickhouse-connect, which overstates its level) would interleave two statements, and with only a connection-level cancel (psycopg) one probe's timeout would cancel another's statement. Waiting for the lock counts against timeout_s; running out while waiting is FL702.

Answers table_exists/columns from the warehouse's own catalog.

An empty answer means the table does not exist (False). When the question cannot be asked or answered (rendering fails, the query fails with FL700, rows lack column_name/data_type) the answer is None (unknown), never False; the error is kept in :attr:errors. columns is also None when the dialect has no native profile, as its type names cannot then be mapped to families.

A timeout (FL702) is not an answer: it is raised, so a caching wrapper does not store a transient failure as "unknown" for its whole TTL.

One query serves one table_exists and one columns call for the same ref: the result is memoised until the other method has used it, or for at most memo_s seconds, so table_exists followed by columns (as CachedCatalog asks) costs one query. The memo is guarded by a lock, so one instance may serve several threads.

Every problem FactLang reports carries a stable code FLnnn. The hundreds digit is the stage that found it:

range stage surfaces as FL1xx lexer a diagnostic; the claim is invalid FL2xx parser a diagnostic; the claim is invalid FL3xx analyser a diagnostic; the claim is invalid (warnings and info do not invalidate) FL4xx planning an error outcome, or a ValueError from plan_for / check_pack FL5xx rendering RenderError; an error outcome in a report, a ValueError from fl.compile FL6xx contract completeness reported by fl.check_pack in your tests FL7xx execution ExecutionError; an error outcome, or Measurement.error

docs.title: Notes on particular codes
docs.text: FL206 A filter is always the last element of a claim, so an attribute written after WHERE is read as part of the filter and fails here. Write attributes first. FL311 versus FL313 A catalog answering "unknown" never produces an error: only a definite "no such table/column" is FL311. FL313 is information that names were not verified. FL404, FL405, FL506 The sampling rules of raw measurement: sampling never reaches a claim, block and row samples need a single read, and a dialect that cannot sample a way says so. FL605 Without this check, a custom verb that forgets filter=claim.filter would answer COUNT orders VALUE ==1400 WHERE status = 'paid' with the count of all orders. FL703 The guard is lexer-free and deliberately over-strict, trusts the connector's dialect label, and does not detect side-effecting functions; credentials are the real boundary. See Metadata SQL. FL7xx are never no_data A query that could not run is a defect to fix, not an absence of data.

docs.title: FactLang grammar (normative)
docs.text: This document is normative for the syntax of FactLang 1.0. Every fenced block tagged factlang-valid is parsed by tests/conformance/test_grammar_doc.py and must parse without errors; every block tagged factlang-invalid FLnnn must report that code. Blocks whose code is FL3xx are checked against the analyser instead (they are syntactically valid). The grammar knows no verbs: the examples use the standard pack only to read naturally.

docs.title: 1. Properties
docs.text:
1. Line-oriented. A claim ends at a newline. A trailing \ continues it on the next line.
  2. A verb is the first token of a claim and must be an all-uppercase identifier.
  3. Attribute names are all-uppercase identifiers. Operands end at the first all-uppercase bare identifier, so an uppercase bare word is never an operand. Quote an uppercase operand: "ORDERS".id.
  4. Keywords are case-sensitive.

An uppercase identifier is an IDENT containing at least one letter and no lowercase letter (MAX_PER_KEY is; _ is not).

docs.title: 2. Lexical grammar
docs.text:
IDENT       = ( letter | "_" ) { letter | digit | "_" | "$" } ;
QIDENT      = '"' { any char except '"' or newline | '""' } '"'
            | "`" { any char except "`" or newline | "``" } "`" ;
NUMBER      = [ "-" ] digit { digit | "_" } [ "." digit { digit } ] [ ("e"|"E") ["-"|"+"] digit {digit} ] ;
PERCENT     = NUMBER "%" ;
DURATION    = digit { digit } ( "s" | "m" | "h" | "d" | "w" ) ;
CARDINALITY = "1:1" | "1:N" | "N:1" | "N:M" ;
STRING      = "'" { any char except "'" or newline | "''" } "'" ;
ARROW       = "->" ;
OP          = ">=" | "<=" | "==" | "!=" | "=" | "<" | ">" ;
PUNCT       = "." | "," | "[" | "]" | "(" | ")" ;
COMMENT     = "#" { any char except newline } ;
CONT        = "\" { " " | TAB } NEWLINE ;

Strings are single-quoted only; double quotes and backticks delimit identifiers. = is a synonym of ==. Ordering: CARDINALITY before NUMBER; DURATION before NUMBER; two-character OP before one-character; -> before - as a number sign. An unexpected character is FL102; an unterminated string or quoted identifier is FL101; a dangling continuation is FL205.

Continuation. A \ followed only by spaces or tabs before the newline joins the next line to the claim (CONT above); the blanks between the \ and the newline are ignored. A \ followed by anything else is FL102, and a \ with no next line is FL205.

docs.title: 3. Syntactic grammar
docs.text:
document   = { line } EOF ;
line       = [ directive | claim ] [ COMMENT ] NEWLINE ;
directive  = "USE" ref ;
claim      = VERB { operand } { attribute } [ filter ] ;
operand    = edge | ref | literal ;
edge       = ref ARROW ref ;
ref        = name { "." name } ;
name       = IDENT | QIDENT ;
filter     = "WHERE" condition ;
attribute  = ATTRNAME [ OP ] value ;
value      = NUMBER | PERCENT | DURATION | STRING | IDENT | QIDENT
           | CARDINALITY | typed | list ;
typed      = ( "DATE" | "TIMESTAMP" ) STRING ;
list       = "[" [ value { "," value } [ "," ] ] "]" ;

Rules enforced by the parser:

  • VERB and ATTRNAME are uppercase identifiers. A first token that is not one is FL203 ("expected a verb").
  • A literal operand is a NUMBER, PERCENT, DURATION or STRING. An IDENT/QIDENT operand is always a ref.
  • Every part of a ref is an IDENT or QIDENT. Anything else after a . (for example a CARDINALITY or NUMBER) is FL203. A part after a dot may be uppercase; only the first token of an operand decides where operands end.
  • An attribute value never starts at WHERE; a missing value is FL201. A repeated attribute name is FL204. An unclosed list is FL202.
  • WHERE is the only reserved word inside a claim. A filter is always the last element of a claim and runs to the end of the line (or continuation). Anything the filter grammar cannot consume, including a later attribute, is FL206.
  • USE is reserved only as the first token of a line, and must be alone on its line apart from a comment. Anything after the ref is FL203. Elsewhere USE is an ordinary attribute name.
  • Comments are kept on the claim or directive they trail. Comment-only and blank lines produce no item.
  • Parentheses, NOT chains and lists share one nesting budget of 64 levels; deeper is FL207.
  • A line with any error produces diagnostics and no item; parsing resumes on the next line.

docs.title: 4. Filters
docs.text:
condition  = conj { "OR" conj } ;
conj       = atom { "AND" atom } ;
atom       = "NOT" atom | "(" condition ")" | comparison | name ;   (* bare boolean column *)
comparison = name OP literal
           | name "IN" list
           | name "NOT" "IN" list
           | name "IS" [ "NOT" ] "NULL"
           | name "BETWEEN" literal "AND" literal ;
literal    = NUMBER | STRING | typed | "TRUE" | "FALSE" ;
  • Precedence, loosest to tightest: OR, AND, NOT.
  • AND OR NOT IN IS NULL BETWEEN TRUE FALSE DATE TIMESTAMP are filter keywords, recognised uppercase only. A bare keyword is never a column name; quote it.
  • The column of a comparison is a single name (IDENT or QIDENT), not a dotted ref.
  • A name standing alone as an atom tests a boolean column: deleted means deleted = TRUE. A bare TRUE or FALSE atom is FL206 (they are keywords): a column named TRUE (uppercase) must be quoted as "TRUE", while a lowercase true is not a keyword and is a valid bare column name.
  • x = NULL is FL206: IS NULL is the only way to test NULL.
  • Inside IN, items are filter literals; a trailing comma is allowed.

docs.title: 5. Valid examples
docs.text:
A bare boolean column as a filter.

ROWS orders WHERE deleted

The live-row filter for a flag that is TRUE or NULL.

ROWS orders WHERE deleted IS NULL OR NOT deleted

A parenthesised bare atom under NOT.

ROWS orders WHERE NOT (paid) AND amount > 0

A table exists.

EXISTS orders

A column exists.

EXISTS orders.customer_id

Symbolic arguments are attribute values.

TYPE orders.total IS decimal

An attribute with an operator.

ROWS orders VALUE >=1000

= is a synonym of ==; _ separators are digit grouping.

ROWS orders VALUE = 1_717

Percentages are ratios.

NULLS customers.email RATE <=5%

No attributes.

DEAD products.legacy_code

UNIQUE orders.id

A composite key is an attribute holding a list.

UNIQUE order_items.order_id WITH [line_no]

Attribute names may contain underscores.

FANOUT order_items.order_id MAX_PER_KEY <=50

Strings are single-quoted.

VALUES orders.status IN ['new', 'paid', 'shipped']

A trailing comma is allowed.

VALUES orders.status IN ['new', 'paid',]

'' escapes a quote.

VALUES orders.note IN ['it''s fine'] ALLOW <=1%

Attributes may follow each other freely.

VALUES events.kind IN ['click', 'view'] SPLIT ':'

BETWEEN is an ordinary attribute name here.

RANGE orders.total BETWEEN [0, 100000]

Typed literals as attribute values.

RANGE orders.created_at BETWEEN [DATE '2020-01-01', DATE '2030-01-01']

RANGE events.at BETWEEN [TIMESTAMP '2020-01-01T00:00:00Z', TIMESTAMP '2030-01-01T00:00:00Z']

Signed, decimal and exponent numbers.

RANGE orders.discount BETWEEN [-1.5, 1e2]

PATTERN customers.email LIKE '%@%.%' RATE >=99%

Durations: s m h d w.

FRESH events.at WITHIN 24h

An edge operand.

JOIN orders.customer_id -> customers.id MATCH >=99%

Cardinality is one token.

JOIN orders.customer_id -> customers.id MATCH >=99% CARD N:1 CAST string

COUNT orders VALUE ==1717 TOLERANCE 0.5%

DISTINCT orders.customer_id VALUE ==42

SUM order_items.price VALUE ==1234.5 TOLERANCE 1%

AVG order_items.price VALUE >=10

MIN orders.total VALUE >=0

MAX orders.total VALUE <=100000

Uppercase words after the operands are attributes.

NOTE customers.age IS years BECAUSE 'self reported'

Quote an uppercase identifier that must be an operand.

EXISTS "ORDERS".id

Backtick and double-quote identifiers; up to four parts.

EXISTS `my shop`."Order Items".id

Catalog, schema, table, column.

EXISTS shop.public.orders.id

A comment runs to the end of the line.

ROWS orders VALUE >=1 # a comment

Comment-only and blank lines produce no item.

# a full-line comment

A filter is the last element of a claim.

ROWS orders WHERE status = 'paid'

ROWS orders VALUE >=1 WHERE status = 'paid'

ROWS orders VALUE >=1 WHERE status != 'void' AND total > 0

AND binds tighter than OR: a = 1 OR (b = 2 AND c = 3).

ROWS orders VALUE >=1 WHERE a = 1 OR b = 2 AND c = 3

NOT binds tightest; parentheses group.

ROWS orders VALUE >=1 WHERE NOT (a = 1 OR b = 2)

ROWS orders VALUE >=1 WHERE status IN ['new', 'paid']

ROWS orders VALUE >=1 WHERE status NOT IN ['void']

The only way to test NULL.

ROWS orders VALUE >=1 WHERE shipped_at IS NULL

ROWS orders VALUE >=1 WHERE shipped_at IS NOT NULL

The AND after BETWEEN belongs to it.

ROWS orders VALUE >=1 WHERE total BETWEEN 10 AND 20 AND status = 'paid'

Booleans are uppercase TRUE / FALSE.

ROWS orders VALUE >=1 WHERE paid = TRUE

ROWS orders VALUE >=1 WHERE created_at >= DATE '2025-01-31'

ROWS orders VALUE >=1 WHERE created_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-01-31T12:00:00Z'

A column named like a filter keyword is quoted.

ROWS orders VALUE >=1 WHERE "IN" = 1

A directive sets the default namespace for later lines.

USE shop.public

USE may carry a comment.

USE public # reporting schema

USE mid-line is an ordinary attribute name.

NOTE orders.total IS currency USE shop

docs.title: 6. Invalid examples
docs.text:
Unterminated string.

```factlang-invalid FL101 ROWS orders VALUE >=1 WHERE status = 'paid 

Unterminated quoted identifier.

```factlang-invalid FL101
EXISTS "orders

Unexpected character.

```factlang-invalid FL102 ROWS orders VALUE >=1 @ 

A `:` outside a cardinality is reserved.

```factlang-invalid FL102
EXISTS orders.a:b

An attribute needs a value.

A bare atom must stand alone; a second name is not an operator.

```factlang-invalid FL206 ROWS orders WHERE deleted deleted 

A bare `TRUE` is a keyword, not a column.

```factlang-invalid FL206
ROWS orders WHERE TRUE

```factlang-invalid FL201 NULLS customers.email RATE 

An operator needs a value.

```factlang-invalid FL201
NULLS customers.email RATE <=

WHERE cannot be a value.

```factlang-invalid FL201 NULLS customers.email RATE WHERE x = 1 

```factlang-invalid FL201
VALUES orders.status IN [,]

A list must be closed.

```factlang-invalid FL202 VALUES orders.status IN ['new', 'paid' 

Also inside a filter.

```factlang-invalid FL202
ROWS orders WHERE status IN ['new'

A claim starts with an all-uppercase verb.

```factlang-invalid FL203 rows orders VALUE >=1 

```factlang-invalid FL203
'rows' orders

A ref part is an identifier or a quoted identifier.

```factlang-invalid FL203 EXISTS orders.1:1 

```factlang-invalid FL203
EXISTS orders.

An arrow needs a right-hand ref.

```factlang-invalid FL203 JOIN orders.customer_id -> 

Operands come before attributes.

```factlang-invalid FL203
ROWS orders VALUE >=1 customers

List items are comma-separated.

```factlang-invalid FL203 VALUES orders.status IN [1 2] 

`USE` must be alone on its line.

```factlang-invalid FL203
USE shop.public MATCH >=1

USE needs a namespace.

```factlang-invalid FL203 USE 

An attribute may appear once.

```factlang-invalid FL204
ROWS orders VALUE >=1 VALUE <=5

A claim continues on the next line after a \, even with blanks after it.

ROWS orders \
  VALUE >=1 \   
  WHERE status = 'paid'

A continuation needs a following line.

```factlang-invalid FL205 ROWS orders VALUE >=1 \ 

Use `IS NULL`.

```factlang-invalid FL206
ROWS orders WHERE status = NULL

A filter needs a condition.

```factlang-invalid FL206 ROWS orders WHERE 

```factlang-invalid FL206
ROWS orders WHERE status =

A filter runs to the end of the line; nothing follows it.

```factlang-invalid FL206 ROWS orders WHERE status = 'a' VALUE >=1 

An uppercase word after a filter is still part of the filter.

```factlang-invalid FL206
ROWS orders WHERE status = 'a' RATE

A filter column is a single name.

```factlang-invalid FL206 ROWS orders WHERE orders.status = 'a' 

Filter keywords are uppercase only.

```factlang-invalid FL206
ROWS orders WHERE status is null

Unclosed parenthesis.

```factlang-invalid FL206 ROWS orders WHERE (a = 1 

A keyword is not a column name; quote it.

```factlang-invalid FL206
ROWS orders WHERE AND = 1

BETWEEN needs AND.

```factlang-invalid FL206 ROWS orders WHERE total BETWEEN 1 5 

`IN` takes a bracketed list.

```factlang-invalid FL206
ROWS orders WHERE status IN ('a', 'b')

Filter literals are numbers, strings, typed dates and booleans.

```factlang-invalid FL206 ROWS orders WHERE rate = 5% 

Unknown verb: reported by the analyser, not the parser.

```factlang-invalid FL300
FROBNICATE orders

Nesting is bounded.

factlang-invalid FL207 ROWS orders WHERE (((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((a = 1)))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))

In a syntax line, [..] is optional, <TYPE> is a value of that type and a|b are the operators the attribute accepts.
